utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Please be seated. The hearing is resumed. Madam Registrar, please have the accused brought in. (Accused brought in)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Are the booths ready? Yes. All the booths? Can everyone hear me, the Defence, the Prosecution? Mr. Blaskic, can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: MR. BLASKIC
utterances.text: Good morning, your Honours, I hear you well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you? We have the assistance with us of the new Registrar. Could she please introduce herself so that everybody knows her?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: My name is Natacha Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: So, Mme Fauveau, you are going to serve Trial Chamber number 1. Without delaying any further, we are going to ask Mme Fauveau to have the witness brought in, Major Baggesen. (Witness entered court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Major Baggesen, good morning, can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President, your Honours. I can hear loud and clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Please be seated. We are going to continue with the cross-examination and I think it is Mr. Hayman who is doing the cross-examination. You may continue, Mr. Hayman. MAJOR LARS BAGGESEN (continued) Cross-examination by MR. HAYMAN (continued)

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, your Honours. Good morning, Major Baggesen.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Hayman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have your diary and any other materials you would like before we continue your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have my diary, but if you are going to question me about some of my reports, I would like to have a copy of those as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, I will try and prompt the Registrar to give those to you before any such questions, but if at any time we are discussing an area where you do not have a document that you would like to have, for the purposes of referring to the document, please stop me and do not hesitate to ask for the document, okay?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you, since your tour in Bosnia ended, have you undertaken any study of the war or of ECMM materials or anything of that sort?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, because after I came back after the mission in Bosnia, I was asked to train the new Danish monitors who were going to the former Yugoslavia, to the European Community monitor mission, and at that time, I had access to see different kinds of reports from that area, so the new monitors should be -- I was able to tell the new monitors how the situation was at the present time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So those were current reports rather than reports from the time-period of your service in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was new reports.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the time-period or timeframe of those reports?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think I trained some of the monitors one year after I came back, because after a year, one of the other monitors had to take over this task, because it was different from when I have been down there. I think it was too long ago for me, so I want some fresh people in to train the monitors.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you believe it was June 1994 approximately when you would have undertaken a review of current ECMM reports about Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you left the theatre, did you undertake any study or review of materials directed at the 1993 timeframe, events in 1993 in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, only the reports we made at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you say that Tihomir Blaskic supported efforts to expand the work of the ECMM in Central Bosnia during your tour?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that both Colonel Blaskic and Hadzihasanovic did their best.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In that regard to facilitate the work of ECMM; is that what you mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but it was not always enough.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You still faced many difficulties, is that what you mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall anything in particular concerning Colonel Blaskic's efforts to promote ECMM involvement in the areas of Vares and Zepce?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember from the Vares area, but for the Zepce area where I had an area of responsibility during my period of time down there, we normally had no contact with Colonel Blaskic because when we were working in that area, there was no tension between BiH and HVO at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If the usher could assist, your Honour, I have a document I would like placed before the witness. It is short, it is in English; I regret I have no translation at this time. The document for the record was provided by the Office of the Tribunal Prosecutor and was identified as a daily summary report dated 19th March 1993. I note that does not appear on the document; that appeared on an index we received, so may I repeat it: daily summary report, 19th March 1993. Major, did ECMM call one of its routine types of reports a daily summary report?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Normally the daily summary report was a report made by the Regional Centre and sent to the headquarters in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am sorry to disturb the usher again, but if we could place this one paragraph of this document on the ELMO, I would like to call your attention to the first couple of sentences of the report and ask you if you have any other information about this issue mentioned in the report. Thank you. Let me read the first couple of sentences, Major, and then I will ask you about them. The document is entitled "Tuzla, Busovaca Commission/Zenica: "The Commission met along with the HRC and the COO ECMM with Colonel Blaskic, HVO. A wide variety of topics were discussed, but the main purpose of the meeting was to familiarise the COO with the issues in the area of RC Zenica. Colonel Blaskic stressed the need for ECMM involvement in the areas of Vares and Zepce in order to continue/stabilise the situations there and to maintain calm in these areas." First, Major, if you could help us, COO ECMM, what would that be a reference to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think the COO ECMM was -- I think it was a staff officer from our headquarters in Zagreb, and if it was not senior operations officer in Zagreb, it could be our own operations officer in Zenica, but because this meeting was before I arrived, I do not know, but I think it could be the senior operations officer from Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you arrived, that is a few weeks after this report was generated and you arrived in the country, did you go during your tour to either Vares or Zepce on behalf of ECMM?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the HVO local commander in Zepce support the efforts of the ECMM?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, actually at that time when I visited that area it seems that it was very calm in that area and I can remember when going to that area we saw there were some checkpoints manned with HVO and BiH in co-operation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you find it odd that within the same operative zone, there were points where co-operation seemed to be so positive between the HVO and the army and yet there were other points where the situation was so poor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the Zepce area and the Zavidovici area and Maglaj area and the northern part of that area we were operating in, it was necessary for the HVO and BiH to work together because this area was surrounded on three sides by the Bosnian Serb Army, so therefore they had to work together, and if not the Bosnian Serb Army would have taken over that area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They would have all perished; is that your point?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you reviewed the documents which gave rise to the Busovaca Joint Commission? That is the founding documents.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have seen that document, but I cannot recall all the details in it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Among that -- within that document or among those documents, was there a joint order from Hadzihasanovic and Blaskic giving certain powers to their deputies and their representatives on the Commission?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot recall that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there times, when you were travelling with the Commission and Mr. Nakic, the Deputy Commander of the HVO in the operative zone was with you, when the group was not allowed to pass through a checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you find that odd, that the Deputy Commander of the HVO in the zone could not get through an HVO checkpoint within his zone of command?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Normally, we did not have problems at those checkpoints I marked at the board last week. Sometimes when we were going to do some fact-finding in one of those areas where there have been complaints, there was maybe a small, newly established checkpoint and sometimes we were not allowed to pass that checkpoint. Then we had to ask Colonel Blaskic's office to have a written order to pass that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you finished your answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that on more than one occasion then that the Busovaca Joint Commission group, including Deputy Commander Nakic, was not allowed to pass through an HVO checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it on several occasions that that occurred?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It happened a few times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us briefly what specific training or study you have received or undertaken concerning the organisation and functioning of armies within the Warsaw Pact or the armies organised according to the Soviet model?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have studied all the Warsaw Pacts, how they were organised, and I have studied how the former Yugoslavia National Army, how they were organised, and actually, we could see that the same type of organisation used in the Yugoslavian National Army, the JNA, was copied to HVO and BiH.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your study of the Soviet model and the JNA, was that formal coursework or independent reading and study? What type of study was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was a study during my training as an intelligence officer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As part of a survey course of different military systems?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Any other study or particularised research you did on either the Soviet military model or the former Yugoslav National Army model?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not think I would be able to tell all this in court, because that is something to do with the Danish Army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I do not want you to reveal any confidential information. Speaking at a very general level, is it other coursework you have received or are you referring to some type of tour or duty that you have had that involved the Soviet or Warsaw Pact model?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think I already had answered that I know how the units were organised.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I do not want you to reveal any confidential information, but I am trying to determine the depth and nature of any studies or training you have received in that area. If you feel you have given a complete answer and you are not able to provide any more information, so be it. How many men under the JNA system of organisation would a captain command?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You know, the JNA, until 1991, there was national service in Yugoslavia, so when we came in 1993, all men that were -- they started in the JNA at 18 so I think in 1993 all men about 20 have done national service in the JNA and so therefore a lot of the soldiers in HVO and BiH have done military service. That included a lot of the officers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You may not have heard my question. My question was: under the JNA model or system of organisation, how many men would a captain command, that is a captain in the JNA would be in command of how many men?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You had a structure where normally a company were around 100 men, battalion level had three, four or five companies and the brigade units had a lot of battalions; it would all depend on what type of brigade it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What type of unit would a captain typically command?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Can you use another word --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For captain? Apparently in the JNA, that position would be known as "capitan", something to that effect. In English it is captain, as in the captain of an ocean vessel.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Denmark a captain is normally a company commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About 100 men then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is in the Danish system?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And normally in all NATO and former Warsaw Pact units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know whether, in terms of training and organising military units within the JNA, was a distinction drawn between the basic training of soldiers and the training of men within units; that is training them to perform as part of a unit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were trained to perform as a part of the unit and actually JNA was one of the biggest armies in Europe, and it was a very -- I think they were very clever, the soldiers in the JNA and well trained.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They emphasised both types of training, is that right, personal basic training and training to operate as part of a unit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know, within the JNA model, what period of training was deemed necessary to train the smallest group of soldiers; that is approximately 10 soldiers, to train them to work as a unit. How long was that deemed to take under the JNA system?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It all depends on what type of units. Normally I think they had to do their national service for a minimum of 12 months and, of course, you have to start with the basic training and all depending on what kind of unit, this basic training was I think two or three months, just where they would teach how to be an individual soldier and after that we were training how to co-operate in an unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you agree that at least in the JNA system, there is a sequential order of training, starting with basic training of the individual, followed by training individual soldiers to function as part of a basic unit of perhaps, say, 10 soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is normally in all armies the world over.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that, is there also a period of training deemed necessary to train members of a platoon to work together; that is a larger unit of soldier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is normally what you are doing; when you are able to co-operate in a small unit then you are trained to co-operate in a bigger unit and after that in a bigger unit again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the progression would be roughly the ten-men unit, then a platoon type of unit --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then a company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then a battalion; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then finally to operate as part of a brigade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sometimes that was at the same time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is they would be teaching those different levels of organisation at the same time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sometimes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know how long within the JNA model it would take to complete all of that training for a given soldier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think they would use most of their national service to train that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which would be about 12 months?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you reviewed any JNA manuals or other materials in that record?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are giving your best answer as you sit here today?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, because that is the normal way for all armies in the world to train like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So your answer is not specific to the JNA; it is a generic answer based on your experience of all militaries?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: First within NATO, the NATO context or NATO language, is an operative zone the same thing as a zone of responsibility, or is there a distinction between those two terms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that the operative zone is the same as the area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is the same as AOR, area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How about in the JNA model? Do you know whether it is the same or whether there was a distinction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was a distinction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the distinction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As I can recall, I do not think the JNA was operating in operative zones, but they had their brigades and their corps level and those units had their own area of responsibility when they are going to a war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the JNA did not have operative zones; that is your recollection?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Not during peacetime. Maybe during wartime they would do something similar to that to give a special unit an area of responsibility, and then you call this type of unit an operational zone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree that within the JNA model, there is a distinction between a corps as a method of organising soldiers or units of soldiers and an operative zone?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the distinction that you would see in those two concepts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because the corps is a unit who have a lot of men and OZ is the area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree that a corps is a tactical group of units?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whereas an operative zone is more of an administrative concept?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that is the area this unit had --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is a geographic concept then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They have their area of responsibility in that specific area. That is normally when you -- in a war, every unit has their own area of responsibilities and the commander there is commander of all the operations inside this AOR.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Within the Danish or NATO model, approximately how many soldiers would exist within a corps? I understand an estimate is probably required. There may be no specific number.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Maybe 10,000 soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To effectively command a corps within the NATO concept, what size of headquarters staff would be required?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You have the commander and the deputy commander and then you will have staff officers who are responsible for the operations, staff officers who are responsible for the intelligence services, staff officers who are responsible for the logistics, transport of men, ammunition and fuel and things like that, and you will have staff officers who are responsible for the administrative work.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you say though -- is this work that can effectively be performed by a headquarters staff of ten, or does it typically require a headquarters staff of a couple of hundred officers to get the work done so there is effective command over that corps?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It all depends what kind of corps, but I think you can have ten high rank officers and then you will have a lot of non-commissioned officers and civilians who are doing a lot of the paperwork.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the minimum number -- if this is not a question you feel you can answer, please say so. Is there a minimum number of professional officers, that is professional, trained officers, to function effectively as a corps headquarters staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think as a minimum the commander, his deputy and staff officers who are responsible for the beforementioned operations and the intelligence and the logistics and the administering of things, they had to be professional soldiers that have been trained at the Military Academy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You think it would only take about seven professional officers therefore to command a corps of about 10,000 men?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, because all the commanders had to be professional soldiers as well, all the brigade commanders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that also true in wartime, that in your opinion, seven professional officers together with brigade commanders, could effectively command 10,000 soldiers within a corps?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. Normally in wartime you will have a lot of officers who have been doing the -- they have been given some officers' training, and they will have been officers prepared and they are in the reserve, so you can bring in those officers who had a former officers' training to be a member of the staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you think in wartime it would take a greater number of officers to effectively run the corps?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Within the NATO model, how many professional officers are typically assigned or attached to the command headquarters staff at the corps level?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then how many non-commissioned officers and other administrative type of personnel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A lot more; I cannot say how many.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Hundreds of NCOs and administrative assistants?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think 50.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Putting aside the issue of communications which we will discuss later, what else is necessary in terms of a headquarters staff and the functioning of a headquarters staff for a commander to exercise effective command?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is necessary for the commander, when he has given his orders, that he controlled -- that these orders were carried out in the way he wants them to be. He can do that himself or he could let one of his staff officers to inspect the soldiers, the units, to see if their orders the commander gave were carried out in the way the commander wanted them to do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about logistical requirements? Does whether or not you have supplies to provide to troops under your command affect the ability of a commander to actually control those troops, money to pay them, guns, those types of things?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We have seen in a lot of armies that getting the money to the troops has been a problem. I think in the former Yugoslavia that was a problem, but I do not think that, especially not for HVO, they had a lot of weapons and equipment from the former JNA, but, of course, when the commander is going to order his units to do something, it is vital that those units had the proper equipment, the proper weapons to carry out those orders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but if troops are not paid, does that affect the ability of a commander to exercise command over those troops?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not in wartime, because when the soldiers are in the front, he does not have anything to use his money for.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about if soldiers are not regularly fed, if they are getting one meal a day, does that affect the ability of the commander to exercise command over those troops?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It all depends on how disciplined the unit are.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If they are not operating at a high level of discipline, would a lack of, for example food, could that affect a commander's ability to exercise command?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it could.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you ever worked in the area of institution building within the military sphere? I can define that term if you would like me to.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you ever for example gone to Lithuania to consult with the army there on how to build a professional effective army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not think I quite understand your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question was whether you personally had ever been involved in any work in the area of institution building, by which I mean the process of building a professional institution or entity such as a well trained, disciplined effective army where none had existed before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, when have you been involved in institution-building within the military sphere?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Denmark, together with other NATO countries, we are going to build up Home Guard units in the Baltic area. We are sending instructors to Estonia and Latvia and trying to building up a new military unit in that area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you personally been involved in those efforts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, just only to do some planning, paperwork, on what those instructors who were going over there -- how they should behave and what sort of training they should give over there. Then we are bringing officers from the countries in the Baltic to Denmark and we train them in Denmark so they are able to go back to their own units and train them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did the programme start?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think just after the Soviet Union was divided.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So several years ago?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is the programme still going on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is. Actually next month I will receive some officers from over there and I have to train them and tell them how to command a Home Guard district.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it a long-term project?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would not say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It has been going on for three to five years; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it scheduled to end soon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I hope.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But I take it you do not know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the intense period of conflict from roughly 16th April to 20th April 1993, did the army hold any civilian prisoners, and if you wish to refer to your diary at page 7, you are free to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Hayman, I would like to know whether you intend to offer this exhibit on the Busovaca group as evidence. I think it has been identified. There may be some doubt as to the date. What is your opinion, Mr. Hayman? Do you want to tender it?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: I will offer it, your Honour, and the date is the date that I read which was provided to us by the Prosecution. Because it is redacted, we do not have a date on the document itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I assume that the Prosecution agrees? Does the Prosecution agree on the date, 19th March 1993? Mr. Cayley?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: I would imagine that the witness, your Honour, is probably the best person to answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: I do not agree with that, your Honour. If counsel does not have a copy of the index they provided to us, I am happy to share it with him. Perhaps if we could hold these exhibits for a moment, I could provide the index to the Prosecutor during the next break and that will eliminate the issue. I am hesitant to burden the witness with these dates.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. Continue then, please, Mr. Hayman.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Major, the question involved civilian prisoners on the army side after the intense conflict in mid-April. Did they have such prisoners?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were prisoners in Zenica and at the 20th April, we visited the prison in Zenica and we saw there was prisoners of war there and we saw a lot of civilians there as well. I cannot recall how many, but as I have mentioned in my diary, they were leaving 25 prisoners in each room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In 60 square feet?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree with the comment that "it was worse than a hen house"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the Danish edition I did not use the word "hen house", but some of the hens are living in very small rooms, and I compare that with this. This was because this was the first prison I visited, and after I visit a lot of the prisons in the area, this was one of the better ones.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Turning your attention to the villages in the area of Zenica, and perhaps while I am raising this subject we could put exhibit 29A on the easel and see if it could be of use.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I could just make a clarification, my learned friend just made a quote from the diary in which he said 60 square feet. If he looks again he will find the measurement is slightly different from that. Perhaps he could correct the position, or the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: I am sorry, were you asking me? Let us do it through the witness, counsel. Major, were the groups of 25 prisoners imprisoned in 60 square metres of space each?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes -- no, not each.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Each group of 25?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, were living in rooms like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Excuse me, a very French question. Is it 60 square feet or 60 square metres? The translation gives me sometimes feet and I must check. This is a third of the metres, so is it 60 square feet or 60 square metres please, Major?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Square metres, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: I would like to ask you about your visit on April 21st 1993 to the village of Zalje in the region of Zenica. Do you recall that visit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you think you would be able to indicate where approximately that village was located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot recall the exact position, but it was in one of the villages in the surrounding area of Zenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you visit this visit with Father Stjepan who you have previously described?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we did and he told us about those incidents, so I have not been an eyewitness to those killed persons, but Father Stjepan, he told us about those persons who had been killed in that area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did he tell you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He told us that ten civilians had been killed, including a young girl who was lying in her bed shot in the head. It also included the murder of an old man of 90 years old.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall: was there a village of mixed ethnicity? What type of village was it? Do you have any recollection in that regard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think most of the villages down there were with mixed population. We were told by Father Stjepan that the unit who did this awful thing were a MOS unit, you would call them Mujahedins.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am not sure the term Mujahedin has been defined. What did people mean in this theatre when they used the term Mujahedin?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: These Mujahedins is not a national unit from Bosnia, but a group of individuals coming from Arabic countries.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So foreign nationals fighting in Bosnia on the side of the army; is that a fair statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not saying on the side, because actually I think they were fighting their own war. I discussed the matter with General Hadzihasanovic, because we complained to the Third Corps about things like this. He told us he was not able to control the Mujahedins but he was going to do his best because all those things that these Mujahedins did down there were harming the Muslim reputation, so therefore he would try to stop them if he was able to do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did those types of atrocities on both sides greatly inflame the situation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not think that this incident inflamed the tension in the area because there was a lot of incidents like this from both sides.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You spoke earlier about the fears of the Croat civilians in the Zenica area. Were there some real fears based on incidents like this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot recall if this incident in Zalje -- I do not think that was the reason that the rumours started later on, but, of course, it happened and people knew about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It would affect psychology and the mental thoughts of those people living in the area; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were asked in your direct examination whether there were troops of the army in the Lasva Valley on April 16th 1993. Do you recall that question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your answer as I recall was no. Have I recalled it properly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As of April 16th, you had been in the theatre about two weeks; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You had been briefed on arrival by ECMM; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you had had one or more briefings from UNPROFOR; is that also correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had some or all of those briefings included the issue of the army and where they were or were not located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, because normally in that area, the British battalion was sending out patrols and they were covering more or less the whole area so they were able to see where there were HVO positions and where there were BiH positions. We have no information about BiH positions in that area near Ahmici for example.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you: did you have occasion to visit the Third Corps headquarters in Zenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was there several times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you learn in the course of those visits how many brigades there were in the Third Corps?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Actually I cannot recall the exact numbers of brigades. I never -- I did not have the opportunity to receive this list when we asked for it, so we had the list from HVO but at that time we did not have the list from BiH.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever get a list from the BiH of the brigades in the Third Corps?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not, but we knew about their brigades. I cannot recall how many and where they were situated. I can remember some of them were situated in Zenica and south of Zenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall whether there were any Territorial Defence Forces in the Lasva Valley as of 16th April 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is you do not recall or you think there were none?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think there were none.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also said you visited the village of Ahmici a few days before the massacre on 16th April. How many days before? Can you give us your best recollection in that regard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Two or three days before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The purpose of your visit was to visit the mosque?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, to see the mosque.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is the mosque in lower Ahmici or upper Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Lower Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go further into the village up the hill than the mosque?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, we did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you visit the school that is slightly up the road and to the left, that is across the street from the mosque?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, we just went to the mosque and we stopped in front of the mosque just to see the mosque.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far up from the road is the mosque? Just an estimate, if you can.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 1,000 metres or less.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On your visit, did you ask anyone any questions about the presence or absence of Territorial Defence or army troops in Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, we did not but I was able to use my eyes and I could see there was no sign of military activity in that part of Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I take it you were not there to look for signs of the military, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You did not ask anyone, for example, "where is the army headquarters?"

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, we did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to read you a list of locations and ask you if you have ever visited the Territorial Defence units in any of these locations. Kruscica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember. I think if you are able to show me on the map, maybe I can recall some of the areas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Kruscica is immediately to the south, immediately, I do not know what the distance, but it is located in a southerly direction from Vitez, do you see it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever visit a TO or Territorial Defence unit in Kruscica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Actually I cannot recall all the areas, but I can remember that we visited some units of the BH in -- I cannot remember, there was one headquarters or something similar in the Vitez area. There was something in the mountains up here, and we visited some in the Busovaca area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you visit a BiH headquarters in Poculica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You do not recall where this headquarters was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember we visited a headquarters in this area here somewhere.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are indicating to the south of Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, south of Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Roughly in the area of Kruscica? I am not trying to tie you to the name of that village, but when you indicated with your finger were you indicating generally in the area of Kruscica and to the south downward on the map of Kruscica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I recall that we visited a unit in the mountains or the hilly area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To the south of Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but it was not that south, it was up here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Not that south, indicating the area of mountains where there are no towns considerably to the south?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was more, not in this direction but in the area here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Between Kruscica and Rovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was that visit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember, it was together with the Busovaca Joint Commission and we had to go out there to see if one of the local agreements was carried out by the local commander in that area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that unit established as of 16th April or do you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot recall the exact period. Maybe it was before 16th April or maybe after, I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you visit a Territorial Defence unit in the town of Gacice, indicating to the west of Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you visit a TO unit in the area of Donja Veceriska, which is to the north-west of Gacice and to the west-north-west of Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How about a TO unit in the village of Vranjska, and in a moment we will try and identify that for you on the map, if we can. I do not know if we are going to be able to identify that one on the map for you, but I take it the name does not mean anything to you in terms of a TO unit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The only thing I can remember is that we visited one small headquarters up here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Indicating to the south of Vitez.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not think -- it was not a brigade headquarters; it was a battalion or company headquarters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that a TO unit or an army unit, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot recall. I can recall that we visited a headquarters and it was a battalion headquarters or a company headquarters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The unit you visited to the north of Vitez, do you remember anything else about that unit? Was it Territorial Defence, was it army, the type of command or headquarters it was, any details?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The only thing I can remember, in the beginning BiH had a small military headquarters in Vitez. I think it was situated in this part of Vitez here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In Stari Vitez? Old Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in old Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So there was an army unit in Stari Vitez as far as you knew?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We saw a headquarters and had a meeting at a headquarters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is within the Lasva Valley, correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me just read a list of other towns and ask you if they refresh your recollection as to any visits to Territorial Defence units that you may have made: Pezici, Poculica, Bukva, Muratovici, Preocica, Tolovici, Lupac, Vrhovine, Sivrino Selo. Do those refresh your recollection at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please be seated. Did you visit, on your tour, any of the three battalions of the 325th Brigade of the Third Corps?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember the names of the different brigades. Maybe, maybe not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Other than the two army or TO locations you have described, one south of Vitez, one north, do you have any recollection of visiting any other army units within the area of the Lasva Valley?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not together with the Busovaca Joint Commission or later on together with my own team.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So at no time, you do not recall any such visits?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that correct that at no time do you recall any such visits?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot recall that any of the other monitor teams have visited headquarters in other areas than those which were mentioned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me just quickly list other units and their locations and ask you if it refreshes your recollection in any way. 306th brigade in Han Bila; 17th Krainja Brigade in Kruscica; 333rd Brigade in the Busovaca municipality, headquartered in Kacuni. Do any of those refresh your recollection at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the last one. I cannot recall if that was the name of the brigade, but I remember visiting a unit in the Busovaca area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: An army unit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the conflict began on 16th April, was a confrontation line or a frontline formed between HVO and army forces?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can remember that we were discussing who was having the control over certain areas in that area. I cannot recall that we were able to draw a strict line on the map, but we learned that HVO were commanding most of the valley including Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Most of the what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Most of the Lasva valley, because we were able to see by the checkpoints manned at the road, so those checkpoints that are marked on the road show that HVO were controlling this area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did those checkpoints exist before the 16th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they did and after the 16th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They did not change as a result of the conflict on the 16th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That showed that HVO was still having a control in that area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I take it that other than that you did not gather any information or receive any information where the confrontation lines or front lines were between the HVO and the army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If the usher could assist, your Honour, Major, you described receiving a letter from the Mujahedin concerning the abduction of Commander Totic and the four HVO officers from the Travnik, Novi Travnik area.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to show you a letter and ask you if you recognise it. I would ask the usher to put it on the ELMO, I think we will need to have a brief sight translation of it. While that is being done, perhaps the Registrar could provide numbers for the last exhibit and for this one, if it is convenient.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This one is D37 and the previous one is D36.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: No objections, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Continue, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: The letter has illegible writing at the very top, at least illegible to me. Then there appears to be some Arabic writing and then, cut off the ELMO at the very top, is the word "Zenica", and then there are certain numbers which speak for themselves: "To whom it may concern. We inform you that all hostages of HVO officers are alive and we want immediate release of all foreign prisoners from HVO prisons in Bosnia. It is to be noted that we have tried many times through your agencies and other responsible organisations to release them, but without any response. So there was no other way left after that, only to take those leaders as hostages and to exchange. We waited long to give chance to such organisations to release our brothers without any bloodshed. So we warn you that if our brothers are not released, we are going to kill all the hostages and for these brothers from foreign countries we inform you that they know their way and good [or God] very clearly, for they came to die as martyrs in the way of Allah alone and nothing else, and that such operations will never be the last. On the contrary it will be the beginning of a series of Jehadic operations and martorious actions which we shall be able to perform with the help of Allah to whom we return and to whom all the order is. Last but not least, you and all other organisations will be responsible for the killing of the hostages and the prisoners." Then there is some further Arabic writing. Do you recognise this letter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I can recall that we received this letter in this version and then a German version as well with the same text and it was handed over to us by a representative from the Mujahedin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The kidnapping of Commander Todic took place on 15th April, do you recall that, 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes I think he was captured after the four staff officers at the Travnik front.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And ECMM did conduct an investigation at the scene of the abduction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I take it you were not one of the members of that investigative team?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Another Danish monitor went to the scene and he saw the scene.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he describe it to you in some detail?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever view a videotape of the scene?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether the scene of the abduction that is videotaped footage from the scene of the abduction was played on the local news in the Lasva Valley on the evening of 15th April 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know, but a lot of the incidents down there were filmed to the local television stations.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have a short tape we would like to play. Perhaps this would be a convenient break, or if you wish to proceed, we will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I think we can have the break now and we will continue at 11.35. (11.15 am) (A short break) (11.35 am)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The hearing is resumed. Madam Registrar, please have the accused brought in. (Accused brought in)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Hayman, I think we interrupted you just when you wished to show the witness a videotape. I assume the technical department is ready so please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour, almost. Let me ask the witness another question or two to set the stage. Were you informed through the ECMM investigation that the abduction involved the killing of four bodyguards and one innocent bystander?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you informed that those individuals, at least the bodyguards, appeared to have first been wounded and then were executed by shots to the head?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, this tape has three segments. I will seek to pause between the segments to ask additional questions of the witness. Regretfully, the first segment is most unpleasant and I wish to apologise to the court for feeling the need to show it, but also to advise the gallery that if there is anyone not wishing to view these scenes, that they should avert their eyes or temporarily leave the gallery.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. You said what is necessary so there is no need for me to repeat it. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Then I would ask the technical assistants to play the tape and I will ask for a pause when we conclude the first segment. We are not asking the translators to try and translate the TV reporter comments at this time, your Honour. (Videotape played)

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Do those appear to be shells, Major, on the ground?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I think it was holsters from the small arms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Spent shells, shell casings? (Videotape stopped)

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you count four bodyguards and one apparent bystander from that tape, Major?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I think the first person we were looking at was the eyewitness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The individual not in uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, and the four persons close to the vehicle were the bodyguards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it your understanding from the ECMM report that the abduction occurred from a vehicle, that is while the vehicle was actually moving?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Actually I think that this vehicle was stopped and then fired on, and I can remember, we discussed the matter we were told about -- I was told about this. I had not seen it at the spot, but we were surprised that the brigade commander was not hurt after seeing the car.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is the screen that was depicted in the tape consistent with the reports that ECMM gathered concerning the incident?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long was Commander Totic an HVO commander in Zenica? How long was he held hostage, if you know? If you wish to refer to your diary on 17th May, you certainly may?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was released together with four other HVO officers, so he has been in Mujahedin custody a day or two less than the other ones.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he released on approximately 17th May?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was released the same day together with other four HVO officers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that on 17th May, as far as you recall?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During his captivity, were his whereabouts known to the ECMM, or was he held in a secret location, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All five of them were held in a secret place to us. We did not know where they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it known whether he was alive or dead?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were told -- as far as I can remember, a videotape was handed over to us or to his relatives showing that he was still alive.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to play the second segment of this tape and ask you if you have seen it and if you can identify it. The audio track, your Honour, I do not think it intelligible at this time, so I would ask that the first five or ten seconds be played and then we can fast-forward to the conclusion of that segment. (Videotape played)

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: There is a point in the tape where the individual takes off his hat; perhaps the technical assistants could take us to that point. (Videotape stopped)

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: While they are doing that, may I ask you, Major, did you receive any information whether Commander Totic sustained any wounds or injuries in connection with the abduction, or do you not recall?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not recall, but I do not think that he had any.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask the technical personnel whether they have located that portion of the segment. If it could be played, your Honour? (Videotape played)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see the wound on the top of his head?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that consistent with a bullet grazing the top of his skull or are you not able to comment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would have to take a closer look. It could be or it could be something else. If it was a bullet maybe it would be a bigger wound, but it could be.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. We can fast-forward to the end of that segment. (Videotape stopped)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you had an occasion to discuss the Mujahedin with General Hadzihasanovic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he say to you on some occasion that the army had done their best to get rid of the Mujahedin but they had not been effective enough in doing so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that sound consistent with what you recall?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. He told us that he wanted to stop this because the activities carried out by the Mujahedin would harm the Muslim reputation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you attend the event at which certain Mujahedin prisoners were freed and exchanged for Commander Totic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did that occur?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can remember that I was releasing the four HVO officers; they were handed over to me in a secure place in Travnik, and -- after that I had the four HVO officers and we went to Vitez, hotel Vitez, Colonel Blaskic's headquarters, where I handed over the four officers to Colonel Blaskic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he grateful for their release?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I hope.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any signs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he thank you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he did and I think that the local TV station was there as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you then proceed to Zenica for the other exchange?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, because it was agreed that the Mujahedins should be released in front of our headquarters in Zenica. I cannot recall where Mr. Totic -- if he was released in Zenica or in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did any of the Mujahedin fighters attend the prisoner exchange event in Zenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Approximately how many?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 100, I think, members of the Mujahedins and maybe members of the 7th Muslim Brigade, who had a headquarters in Zenica, at the music school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any connection insofar as you knew between the 7th Muslim Brigade and the Mujahedin fighters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We did our best to find out if there were any connections, but as I have told the court before, the 7th Muslim Brigade were acting very Islamic, so therefore they have some connection in their beliefs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With the Mujahedin fighters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But that was the extent of the connection you were able to determine?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would ask the technical personnel to play the third segment of the tape, your Honour. (Videotape played)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall, Major, how many Mujahedin fighters were exchanged for the five HVO officers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 15, I think. No, 13.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise the vehicle with the blue patch?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that was one of our vehicles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By "our" you mean ECMM?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise this scene?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I think that was in the front of the International Hotel where we had our headquarters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that appear to be the same individual who was on the second segment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: That concludes the tape. (Videotape stopped)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the Mujahedin have a permanent headquarters anywhere or were their whereabouts generally secret?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We did not know anything about the headquarters. We think that they maybe had something --

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: It is just a small point, Mr. President. The first video clip was identified by my learned friend as coming from TV Vitez. I wondered if he could just identify to the court the source of the other two clips.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: I cannot, your Honour. I do not know as I stand here the source -- that is who filmed the second and third segments. Commenting on whether the Mujahedin had a headquarters that was known to ECMM?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we think that in Zenica, they had maybe a headquarters or something at the music school in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you visit that location on any occasions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, later on when I was chairing this Joint Humanitarian Commission when we were looking for detained persons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did it appear to be a headquarters of at least some Mujahedin fighters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It could be, because we saw some banners with Arabic words on it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any personnel there who you believed to be Mujahedin fighters, at the music school when you visited it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Actually, I was the only one who was allowed to go in and visit the rooms in the music school. The BiH members of the commission were not allowed to go in there, the HVO members were not allowed to go in there, so I was the only one who was allowed to go inside and see the area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This music school was located in the city of Zenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether the specific perpetrators of the Totic abduction were ever identified or any actions taken to try and identify those individuals?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now I would like to turn to the subject matter of communications. You said in your testimony that the telephone line at one point in time in Kiseljak was cut so that Zenica could not communicate with Sarajevo. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it a normal tactic in warfare to cut your enemy's communication lines?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A basic tactic, would you agree?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You travelled to Kiseljak on a number of occasions during your tour; you have described them. Did you ever see Colonel Blaskic in Kiseljak on one of your visits to Kiseljak?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot recall to have seen Colonel Blaskic in Kiseljak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you ever told that he had a headquarters staff in Kiseljak?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We knew that there was a headquarters in Kiseljak, but we did not know if it was a headquarters connected to Colonel Blaskic himself. We knew there was a local HVO brigade headquarters in Kiseljak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did that brigade headquarters occupy the Kiseljak barracks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you ever told specifically that Colonel Blaskic maintained a headquarters staff at Kiseljak barracks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see any evidence that he did, whatever those indicia might be?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, but we knew from some of the persons, the Croats in Kiseljak, that it was possible to go from Vitez to Kiseljak, passing the mountain and using the small roads and paths.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, when you went to Kiseljak during your tour, how would you get there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Normally we used two different roads. We could use the Busovaca road from Vitez through Busovaca and down to Kiseljak and we could use another road where we were actually following the river through Visoko and that way down to Kiseljak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a route that you normally used?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Normally we used both of them, but sometimes it was difficult for us to pass the Busovaca road because of the checkpoints in that area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What army or armies had checkpoints on the road from Busovaca to Kiseljak along the direct route, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Both parties had, but I cannot recall as I told you last Friday -- I cannot recall the exact positions, but HVO had checkpoints there and BiH had -- I think BiH had the centre part.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am going to approach and perhaps looking at the map could help refresh your memory.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, may I approach the witness? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Would you agree that on this map, exhibit 29E, it reflects the town of Busovaca, indicating where I am currently pointing, the town of Kiseljak where I am currently pointing and a road that traverses in a fairly direct manner between the two?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you also see on this road the location marked Kacuni?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which is about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Five kilometres from Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps a fourth of the way from Busovaca towards Kiseljak?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then if you were to traverse another fourth of the way, you come to a location denominated Bilalovac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any recollection whether the stretch of this road from Kacuni to Bilalovac was held by the army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This area was held by -- controlled by the army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Indicating this area from Bilalovac to Kacuni?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that true during your tour?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As I can recall, we had to use -- because we had a lot of problems in the roads, sometimes there were landmines on the roads, so therefore we felt more secure taking this long way here down to Kiseljak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By "the long way", you are indicating following the Lasva river near Kakanj and then down in a south-easterly direction to Visoko?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then from Visoko to Kiseljak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then from Visoko in a south-westerly direction to Kiseljak?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The only problems we had here was this was very close to the Bosnian Serb Army positions and normally they would fire at us when we passed this area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The portion south of Visoko?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Normally we had to pass this at high speed because the Bosnian Serbs were firing at us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. In the Visoko area, do you recall who controlled that road, as you would travel south from Visoko?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As I can recall, BiH controlled that road, and we normally had no problems using that road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Except for the Serb artillery?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Just for the Serb artillery or their snipers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you come to learn that, in addition to the road from Kacuni to Bilalovac being held by the army, that the telephone lines from Busovaca to Kiseljak were cut?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot recall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever use a landline, and by "land line" I am referring to a telephone that uses physical wire on the ground; did you ever use a landline while you were in Kiseljak to call Busovaca or Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot recall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall ever speaking with Colonel Blaskic on a landline phone while you were in Kiseljak?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said something about a mountain path. Can you elaborate? What were you saying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were told by the Croats in Kiseljak that it was possible to go from Kiseljak to Vitez using the small roads in the mountain, but we did not do that because we did not want to risk ourselves or vehicles going on the small roads.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You felt it was too dangerous a possible route; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, and that was normally for all, including UNPROFOR down there, because a lot of the small routes could be mined, by both sides.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On a small remote road, you might be very vulnerable to an ambush; is that true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, true. If you are not having the control of that area, but as we were told, the HVO were controlling that area, so you were able to go from Kiseljak to Vitez in an area controlled by HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who told you this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were told that in Kiseljak by HVO.
