We are now in the re-examination stage and it seems to me quite normal that the Prosecutor wishes to study the document in accordance with the strategy of the Prosecution, therefore I think there is no problem. Do you intend to have the whole document read, Mr. Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: No, your Honour. In respect of all the documents it will be portions omitted by my learned friend. I think, for the sake of completeness and fairness, other parts of the document should be admitted which are material to the Prosecutor's case.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: I would like them read in their entirety, your Honour, because otherwise there is no end to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Hayman, the question has been decided. I am going to repeat, but not again: this document was tendered by you and it is quite normal that the Prosecution should use that document when his turn comes. You have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Thank you Mr. President. If you could just read from where it states "for the attention of" to where it says "to be notified" in brackets. I do not want you to read the entire document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "For attention of commanders to HVO Brigades; Independent Units", and those included: "Motorised Division, 4th Light Artillery Rocket Division, Vitezovi Special Taskforce, Vitez Military Police 4th Battalion, Chief of Travnik Police Department, Chief of Travnik Defence Department, and HVO Presidents to be notified."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are these the persons to whom Colonel Blaskic was addressing this order?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I could now ask you to refer to the order dated 22nd April 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Will you please tell me the date again?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 22nd April 1993. That is D43A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: D43, is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: That is correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Go ahead, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If you could again read, this is the order dealing with citizens' property, to whom this order was addressed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is addressed to the brigade commanders of Brigade Number 1 to Brigade Number 12, and commanders of individual units, and this includes the 4th Light Artillery Rocket Division, Motorised Division, 4th Battalion Military Police, Vitezovi Special Taskforce and the Communication Company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could go to the end of that document and again where the copies are notified, could you just read that to the court?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "One copy to the addressee, one copy to ONO (operation and training body) and one copy to the files."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again that order is signed and stamped Tihomir Blaskic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could go now to the final document, which is Defence exhibit 44A, to whom is this order addressed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To commanders of all units in Central Bosnia Operative Zone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you go to the end of this document, again there are copies to whom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "One copy to the addressee, one copy to ONO (operations and training body) and one copy to records."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Major Baggesen, all these orders together, does this strike you as a commander who is not able to communicate with his subordinate units?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. Actually all these orders show that Colonel Blaskic was commanding all the units because all those units are mentioned as the address at the top of the orders and it shows that he had an operation and training body, and all those orders to all those units show that he was able to communicate, because if he was not able to communicate, he was not able to give out orders like this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have the orders in front of you. The order dealing with citizens' property is of 22nd April; the order dealing with the treatment of civilians and prisoners is of 24th April and the order dealing with prevention of uncontrolled conduct of commanders and individuals is of 24th April. Are they all subsequent to the events that happened in Ahmici and Vitez that you witnessed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, all these orders are after that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So they are orders after the event?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If I may just have a moment, Mr. President? (Pause).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Cayley, are you ready?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: I am, Mr. President and I only have a few more questions so I think we will be able to complete with this witness today. Major Baggesen, while you were serving in Central Bosnia, did you ever compare your command at home with the command of Colonel Blaskic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did at several times; I compared my unit with both Colonel Blaskic's unit and General Hadzihasanovic's unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you do that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Looking at my own units, a lot of my soldiers they are all, except my staff, part-time soldiers. A lot of them have been doing national service in the Danish Army and some of them are coming to the Home Guard without any military background, and then we trained them. What we saw down there was that HVO and BiH had a lot of soldiers who had been in national service because in Bosnia -- in the whole Yugoslavia, all men had to do 12 months' national service in the JNA until 1991, so therefore I think the biggest part of the soldiers in BiH and HVO had the military training from JNA, and then they have the young ones who enlisted after 1991, after the JNA did not exist, then to train those and give them basic military training.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So a large number of the soldiers in HVO and BiH had done basic military training in the JNA; is that what you are saying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I believe the soldiers you command in Denmark are also part-time soldiers, are they not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How much basic training do you give them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The ones who have no military background, we train them in the beginning for one week and during this week, we give them the necessary training how to use their personal weapon, we train them in first aid, we train them in their own protection against nuclear, biochemical and chemical weapons and we give them lessons in the law on armed conflicts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You do this all in a week?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After this time you issue a weapon to them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They keep that weapon at home, do they not, in the Danish Home Guard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, together with the ammunition and the rest of the equipment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any problems with the soldiers by keeping their weapons at home? Do any soldiers misuse those weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I can only recall one incident in one part of the country years ago, but no incidents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why do you think that is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because we teach them that they have to take care of those weapons and those ammunitions, so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have answered my question. In your view, is it simply enough for a commander to issue a written order and do nothing else, or is an officer normally expected to actually follow up on the orders that he issues to ensure they are being obeyed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is the normal and correct way to do it. Normally when I as a commander am giving an order, I will control that this order is carried out in the way I wanted it to be carried out, and I will normally do that to inspect my troops or I will let one of my staff officers do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have, I think, 16 companies under your command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 17 companies, I apologise. Do you sometimes actually attend a company exercise by surprise, just to see that your orders are being carried out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is the normal way to do it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you regularly monitor what is going on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In terms of Central Bosnia, training, there was a war going on, was there not, so it may well have been that there was insufficient time to train soldiers. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not all the time, because there was a lot of calm periods down there where the soldiers were not at the front, so during those calm periods, they were able to train the soldiers, because they did not have to use all the men at the front. You could have maybe some of the soldiers at the front and the rest could be back in their barracks being given the proper training there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Other than Ahmici and Vitez, did you witness any other military operations involving the HVO and the BiH?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Me myself, I monitored the situation in the Kakanj area where BiH and HVO were engaged.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Other than that, have you ever witnessed what you would term a military engagement between two forces in Central Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were HVO troops doing the rest of the time you were in Central Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Major Baggesen, from your experience as a professional officer, 20 years, and your knowledge of the Danish Army and of other armies in Europe, have you ever known of a colonel who is promoted to a general who is not able to perform his duties properly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you ever known of a colonel who was unable to have his orders carried out by junior officers under his command who was subsequently promoted to a general?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you ever known of a colonel who was unable to discipline the troops under his command who was subsequently promoted to a general?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you ever known of a colonel who failed to carry out the instructions of his political masters who was promoted to a general?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I have not.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: I have no further questions for the witness, Mr. President, but I would ask that the court address one matter and that is in respect of exhibits D42A, D43, D39 and D44, which were orders which were submitted into evidence by my learned friend and, if they are being admitted by the Defence, the Prosecution would request that an admission be made now by the Defence that these are in fact documents that were signed by their client, that the author of these documents is Colonel Blaskic, and the Prosecution would like that admission on the transcript of the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I think there should be no difficulty, because the Defence itself underlined that these documents were signed by Colonel Blaskic. Mr. Hayman?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, there is no dispute here, but, as a matter of principle, we are not here to answer the Prosecutor's questions in their case. We offer documents: they can object or they can not object, and this no man's land in between is quite bizarre. I have never seen it before.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, a final comment. We are not objecting to these documents. We are merely saying that the Defence tendered them; they tendered them to show that their client was issuing certain orders to prevent certain types of conduct. If they admit them for that purpose, they must by inference be saying that their client is the author of these documents. All the Prosecutor would respectfully request from the court is they be asked to make a formal admission on the transcript that these documents were signed by their client.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Hayman, Mr. Prosecutor, the Trial Chamber has noted that these exhibits were tendered by the Defence, were signed by Colonel Blaskic which is not at all disputed by the Defence, I assume, Mr. Hayman? It is not disputed?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: They speak for themselves. My point was: we are not here to answer the questions of the Prosecution nor to testify on behalf of our client in the Prosecution's case. His opportunity to testify will come in the Defence case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Listen, I think that the evidence was tendered by the Defence, it was signed by General Blaskic, the exhibits speak for themselves, they were signed by General Blaskic. I think the incident is closed. Have you any further questions, Mr. Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: No, thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. I turn now to my colleagues. Judge Riad, do you have any questions to put to the witness please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Major Baggesen, I am sorry to impose on you some questions; you must be tired by now, because I am. Just some questions concerning the exhibit D43 which relates really to a more general idea which you exposed when you said that the commander has to check whether his orders are carried out, this is part of his responsibility. I want to ask you: if he discovers they are not carried out, what should his attitude be?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then, your Honour, he had to speak with the commander who is not willing to fulfil this order and if that is not enough, to replace the commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To continue this question with the exhibit D43, which is the order rendered on 22nd April 1993, paragraph 3 which in particular was read: "The most stringent measures shall be taken against violators of this order, pursuant to the regulation book on military discipline." First, this order was rendered after the incident of Ahmici, was it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So all what could be considered as violations were already committed. To your knowledge, has any adequate measure been taken towards those who committed it and who violated this order?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You do not know. You also mentioned cases, I think last week and perhaps today too, in which you were sometimes confronted with obstacles from HVO personnel, whether at checkpoint or whether that incident happened when you spoke of this military conversation, if you remember.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thanks to the intervention of General Blaskic when you addressed yourself to him, that was solved.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know of any other cases where, having addressed yourself to him, the situation was not solved? Was his order always obeyed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can recall if we had had problems, and we told this to Colonel Blaskic, he was able to solve the problems for us. I cannot recall that we have not been able to do anything having this written order from Colonel Blaskic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like just to ask another more general question that is just a clarification, concerning the ECMM weekly summary which you presented to us, I think. This is just for my own knowledge. In paragraph 15, it reads as follows: "The declared position of the Bosnian Croat authorities to implement the Vance-Owen Plan forcing the Muslim population to leave the so-called Croat provinces provoked a reaction which resulted in strong and brutal fighting with actions against the civilian population, especially in the Zenica and Vitez regions." Could you perhaps clarify this a little bit? Who reacted and what was this provoked action and how do you relate it with the brutal fighting? What was the other alternative?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Can I see the document, your Honour, just to recall --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I do not know what number it is. Perhaps I can send it to you, because I do not have a number on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: It is maybe exhibit 90. I think it is 90.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, it is exhibit 90.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What was happening during this period was that we mentioned this, that HVO wanted to, actually to get rid of all the Muslims in province number 10 and therefore they started all the ethnic cleansing to get the Muslims -- to scare them out of the 10th province.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: You seem to relate that to the Vance-Owen Plan.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, because the Vance-Owen Plan told that province number 10 should be governed by the Croats, and therefore the Croats wanted to have an ethnically clean province, therefore they scared the Muslims out of province number 10. That was our conclusion, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because in another moment, you said you opposed the Vance-Owen Plan.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So I think it was the Vance-Owen Plan which provoked the whole thing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. That is my personal conclusion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But did the Vance-Owen Plan proclaim it as an ethnically pure department?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it did not, but that was how the Croats who were going to govern this province -- this was their reaction because they wanted it like that. That is my own personal view on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Major.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Judge Shahabudden?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEN
utterances.text: Thank you. Major Baggesen, I invite your attention to an interesting piece of cross-examination which was directed to establishing a certain distinction; on the one hand it was put to you that you could have a military force whose functions were purely tactical; on the other hand you could have a military force which was also exercising administrative functions within a defined geographical area. Do you recall that piece of the evidence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I imagine there can be some plasticity in modelling these arrangements. Can you have a situation like this in which you have a military force which is exercising tactical functions but within a defined geographical area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us turn a little to the relationship of General Blaskic to those who were superior to him. You said, I thought, that on occasion, he would communicate with General Petkovic in Mostar; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would he communicate with General Petkovic directly, or would he have to go through some intermediary in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that Colonel Blaskic has access directly to General Petkovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He had direct access?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, and that is the normal on this command level; the commanders can speak with each other.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So within his operational area, in Central Bosnia, General Blaskic had no superior; he would relate to General Petkovic away in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us look at the relations of General Blaskic below him. You showed the court a document which I have marked 98; I hope I am not in error. That is why I have shown it up, that document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can recognise the document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is a list of brigade commanders serving, I believe, under General Blaskic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Two of them interest me. You have a column entitled "Vitez Brigade". Do you see that column?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the next box there is the name Mr. Mario Cerkez.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I take it that Mr. Cerkez was therefore the brigade commander in the Vitez area serving under General Blaskic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see that in the fourth box his place, I take it that means his place of work, was at the Vitez cinema; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So we are getting the structure. Then three columns below, horizontally, we have a reference to the Ban Jelacic brigade. In the last box we have Kiseljak barracks. That again was intended on this scheme to demonstrate that Kiseljak barracks was commanded by someone who related directly to General Blaskic. Was that the scheme?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I come to something else. You made the interesting remark earlier today to the effect, I hope I do not misquote you, that in those areas in which the BiH and the HVO were in confrontation with the Serbs, the tendency was for the BiH and HVO to co-operate; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That applied for example to a case in which the BiH and the HVO were, as you said, surrounded by the Serbs. Did Serbs surround the Vitez/Ahmici area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they did not. They were in position further north of that area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you about your testimony about the replacement of an HVO commander. I wonder if you remember it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were cross-examined on the point of some interest as to whether you had mentioned that in your diary or in your written reports.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have not, because this was an incident some of the other monitors, one of the other teams, told me that they have been -- they were going to that area near Kiseljak and Kresevo and they were going to have a meeting with this HVO commander whose name I cannot recall and they were told that he was replaced because he did not want to carry out this order to attack a village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So matters of that kind you did not note in your diary or in your written reports?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, because it was not my area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I turn to exhibit 89A. It is entitled "Routine Team Tasks". It says that the tasks allocated to each team within its own area of responsibility will usually be, (iii): "Routinely liaise with military authorities of the HVO, BiH Armija, BSA and UN as appropriate." You recall that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want you to focus on the HVO and the BiH Armija. There was a conflict, as we know, between the Bosnian Croats and the Bosnian Muslims. Your task, I imagine, was to assist in reducing the level of tension between those two groups if you could; am I right, general?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct and we tried to make local cease-fires.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the course of discharging those responsibilities, you would occupy yourself, for example, with making cease-fire agreements, is that right, or promoting them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you had to promote the making of a cease-fire agreement between those two groups, would you think it sufficient to have as the two parties someone on the side of the HVO and someone on the side of the BiH, or would you also want to bring in other informal armed groups and have them sign the document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Normally when we did things like that it was not on a local level; normally it involved Colonel Blaskic and General Hadzihasanovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see, the two principal parties, as it were.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, both of the two commanders signed this agreement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I turn to exhibit D45, the document signed by your colleague Mr. Landry, I think. It was the penultimate paragraph which I think was read out by counsel to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The one in which Mr. Landry said that he was informed by the HVO headquarters in Vitez that Colonel Blaskic was not available, and then there was some discussion as to whether that meant he was not in the premises or he might be elsewhere, but not within access. It goes on: "I cannot recollect to whom I spoke. I was not told where Colonel Blaskic was, nor where I could get in touch with him." What would that sentence bring to your mind: "I was not told where Colonel Blaskic was, nor where I could get in touch with him."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because if they told us where we were able to contact Colonel Blaskic, they had to tell us where they had their forward headquarters, I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In other words, would that sentence signify to your mind that Colonel Blaskic was in the hotel Vitez or was out of the hotel Vitez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Out of the hotel Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I come to exhibit D42A, dated 17th March. The rubric was read out by you a little earlier. I want you to focus on two things and to explain them to me. The document is issued "for the attention of commanders to HVO brigades, independent units". What might be the meaning of that term, "independent units"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As I see it, the independent units are commanded directly by Colonel Blaskic. They are not belonging to one of the brigades but they are having their orders directly from Colonel Blaskic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Directly from him. Now, two lines down we have a reference to the Vitezovi special taskforce. Did you see that Vitezovi special taskforce?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Hayman asked me in the beginning of his cross-examination if I have ever seen this unit called Vitezovi or another unit called the Jokers. I have maybe seen them, but I have not been aware if they were belonging to --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This suggests too that whatever it was it was within the command of Colonel Blaskic, does it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No doubt about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, good. Would that also apply to the next document, D43A, which was also addressed inter alia to the Vitezovi special taskforce. That document would likewise suggest to you that the Vitezovi special taskforce came within the command of Colonel Blaskic, would it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, and it says as well that he commanded the communications.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want you to pause there as I ask you this: these documents were all issued after 16th April. On the 16th, you were in communication with General Blaskic's headquarters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About this matter. Was there any publicity given on that day or the next day to the events which took place in Vitez and in Ahmici? Was there any TV coverage or so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot recall if there were any television --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Pardon? I did not get that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot recall if there have been any TV stations covering this. I can remember that the day after, after I think M Thebault, together with the head of the ECMM in Zenica -- Ambassador Thebault, together with the -- with the commander of the British Battalion, they went to Ahmici and this was covered by Sky News, one of the international TV stations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So there was some international coverage then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, and actually I think that these orders are a result of all this because Colonel Blaskic was aware of all -- that the whole world was looking at this incident.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I did not ask you that, Major. That is an inference that the court may wish to consider, one way or another, later on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. In one of the documents, Colonel Blaskic enjoined his subordinate officers to arrest any malfeasors, any violators of the laws of international humanitarian justice. You answered my colleague, Judge Riad, by saying that you did not know whether any steps had been taken. Is that a correct rendering of what you said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I put it differently then to you. As you were in touch, you or your organisation was in touch with the HVO at high level over these developments, if any steps had been taken by the HVO to discipline any violators, would that have come to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think maybe we would be able to see the result of that, but we were not informed about what they did, so I do not know if they carried out this particular piece.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you say you were not informed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If any steps had been taken; that is the position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. The last document before me is, I think, exhibit 39A. That opens with the words in the operative paragraph -- I wonder if I am misleading you so I had better hold up my paper to you so you can see visually what I have in mind. It is a document issued by General Blaskic dated 24th April. I have annotated it 39A.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have it here, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It opens with the words "Based on the request by the Chief of the HVO Main Headquarters, reference number of 22nd April 1993." Who was that Chief of the HVO Main Headquarters as mentioned by General Blaskic here?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think Colonel Blaskic is referring to General Petkovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Pardon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think, your Honour, that Colonel Blaskic is referring to General Petkovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In Mostar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEN
utterances.text: I see. Thank you very much, Major.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I have one or two questions because everyone is tired, you first of all and then the interpreters as well. Regarding the questions put to you by the Prosecution making a comparison between the Danish Army, your own Home Guard that you were in charge of, the army of the BH and the HVO, you were saying that it was a professional army that had undergone professional training; therefore you said that it was an organised army regarding the HVO; are we agreed? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not say --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I just want to know whether I am not mistaken regarding your interpretation when you made a comparison between Western armies and the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the structure of the HVO. I think that you said that they could be compared in terms of military organisation and training; am I right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but I did not say that it was a professional army. I was comparing an HVO unit and BiH unit with my unit who are consisting of part-time soldiers and the biggest part of those soldiers had had national service in the army, so a lot of the soldiers --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have understood, yes, you already said that, so I do not want you to repeat it. I am focusing on a rather important problem. You spoke about training in Denmark, regarding the law on armed conflicts.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to know whether during your mission in Central Bosnia you had the impression that the soldiers which comprised the HVO and the BH-Army, but I am focusing on the HVO; did they have occasion to have any training on international humanitarian law and specifically the law on armed conflicts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not think they had that training.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. My second and last question: before 17th March, the series of orders that have been conveyed to us, did you have the impression or the knowledge that Colonel Blaskic gave any orders similar to these before the attack took place? Colonel Blaskic, later General Blaskic, did he pass any orders to prevent such incidents or do you have the impression that these were isolated and that they were issued in the period that followed these incidents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that these orders were only given after 16th April. We have not seen or we have not been told about similar orders given before that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have the impression that in an organised army, this type of order would be given at the beginning of a conflict or in the preparations for a conflict? Does it seem to you to be normal that a colonel with important responsibilities should give orders of this kind?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, this order, Mr. President, should have been given on a more earlier stage at the conflict.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: That is it. Very well, thank you, commander, for your contribution to the International Criminal Tribunal. The court wishes to thank you once again. We are going to adjourn for today and meet again tomorrow at 10.00 am. I should like to remind you, I think, that the Registrar has already told the Defence that we will finish work on Wednesday evening. I hope that has already been communicated to the parties. The meeting is adjourned until tomorrow at 10.00 am. (The witness withdrew) (6.15 pm) (Court adjourned until 10.00 am the following day) 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
